canonical_topic: Uranium Fuel Constraints and Proliferation Risk
definition: The practical and geopolitical limits on sourcing and refining uranium fuel for nuclear reactors.
core_idea: Concentrated uranium is highly toxic and economically extractable only from a limited number of large deposits, and because refining it resembles the process for weapons-grade material, new reactor construction carries proliferation concerns.
key_points: Uranium is highly toxic once concentrated
Large, economically extractable deposits are geographically limited despite uranium being common in the Earth's crust
The refining process overlaps with the process used to produce nuclear weapons fuel
This overlap ties reactor construction to weapons proliferation concerns
relationships: Related to nuclear plant heat generation via fission
